Oil Prices Climb Higher
 
Plus, 10-year Treasury yield briefly hits 2007 levels and the Senate deals a blow to crypto industry
 
By Heard on the Street Staff
 
 
A crude oil storage terminal in Cushing, Okla.  NICK OXFORD/BLOOMBERG
 

This is an edition of the Markets P.M. newsletter, a recap of the day’s most important markets moves, delivered after the closing bell. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

What Happened in Markets Today

 

Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil, gained about 2%, topping $108 a barrel. The closure of a critical Saudi pipeline is pressuring supply, sending prices higher and stoking inflation fears. Chevron Chief Executive Mike Wirth cautioned that global supplies are running low, with no respite in sight.

 

Treasury yields continued their ascent. The yield on the 10-year Treasury rose as high as 5.04%, its highest level since 2007, before paring gains.

 

The crypto industry’s top legislative priority failed in the Senate. The bill would have taken most crypto trading out of the purview of securities regulators. Coinbase shares dropped 10%. Bitcoin fell below $76,000, down almost 4% on the day.

 

CoinEx said it was shutting down. The crypto exchange was the subject of a Wall Street Journal article in June that showed how it had become a favorite of Iranian users, including ones with ties to the Islamic Republic.

 

Major stock-market indexes fell. The Nasdaq declined 0.8%, the Dow industrials lost 0.6% and the S&P 500 slipped 0.5%.

One Big Story

 
 
Kevin Warsh and President Trump at the White House in May AL DRAGO/BLOOMBERG NEWS
 

President Trump spent last year demanding rate cuts from the Federal Reserve. Investors now expect his handpicked chairman to reverse course and start raising them this week.

 

The case for raising rates is a measure of how much the outlook has shifted since Kevin Warsh took over the central bank in May. The war with Iran has gone on longer than officials and investors expected and has pushed energy prices higher. New tariffs have taken effect. The AI build-out has strained supply chains for electricity and technology equipment, adding to demand faster than it has added to the economy’s capacity to meet it.

 

That leaves Warsh facing the fight Trump hoped he would avoid when he selected the new chairman.

 
 
 

What’s Coming Up

 

• Economic reports due Wednesday include retail sales, import prices and manufacturing inventories. The National Association of Home Builders is scheduled to release its Housing Market Index.

 

• The Federal Open Market Committee is scheduled to release its decision on interest rates at 2 p.m. Wednesday.

 

• Companies set to release quarterly results include Lennar and Seabridge Gold.
